author. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, recent scientific studies have shown that fish are sentient animals: they have a complex nature and a rich sensory world and they can experience emotions, but not only that, they also have important cognitive abilities. unfortunately, however, perhaps because of their complexity and mystery, fish have always been underestimated, often ignored and excluded from the protection afforded to other categories of animals. fish are also the most exploited and used animal species. to give you an idea of the phenomenon, some estimates put the total catch at 111 billion fish and the total aquaculture fish at 1.7 billion. these data relate to the european union only. i personally find it almost difficult to assimilate and rationalize the magnitude of these figures. in view of this, we have a strong responsibility towards them, the same as we have towards other animals. however, fish welfare legislation is minimal, and we are far from implementing the measures needed to ensure compliance with international and european animal welfare standards. this is confirmed by the numerous efsa opinions (scientific opinions drawn up by our agency), the repeated evidence of the inadequacy of the implementation of regulation (ec) no 1/2005 on the transport of live animals and of regulation (ec) no 1099/2009 on the protection of animals at the time of slaughter, and also a study by the european commission itself carried out last year. in view of the above, the commission's inaction is no longer justifiable. we need objective, science-based standards, we need high european standards. the possibility of setting minimum requirements through voluntary measures at member state level and on the initiative of industry itself has so far led to very little progress and the little that has been done at times is also disappointing. on the basis of these considerations, we therefore call on the european commission to introduce uniform standards on the animal welfare of fish and to ensure that european legislation is actually respected and implemented.
on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i take the floor again, this time on behalf of my political group and the five star movement. i am reporting on the views of european citizens, because 79% of the citizens want fish to be better protected than they are at present and to be extended to at least the level of protection we already guarantee to other animals that many of them eat. in addition, nine out of ten people believe that painless slaughter is an essential aspect of fish welfare and so these seem to me to be unequivocal figures that the commission can no longer ignore. secondly, there are other things that should not be ignored: there are public health considerations. animals that are kept in unsatisfactory conditions in overcrowded facilities are stressed animals, they get sick more easily, and all of this leads to more use of chemicals, antibiotics, to deal with and contain disease outbreaks. thirdly, the lack of animal welfare standards also has a number of environmental consequences. i am referring, for example, to the algal blooms, the creation of so-called dead zones, real dead zones near aquaculture sites, with possible effects on natural fish resources and biodiversity. i mean, it's time to get active. i think the european commission should do more. the commissioner's answer is unsatisfactory. there are many things that can be done, apart from of course introducing stricter standards and enforcing existing ones: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the drafting of the new directive on the protection of the environment. in conclusion, i cannot but be very dissatisfied and saddened that this house has decided not to make a political resolution to put in writing what we are saying to you today.
author. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today we open this debate on the situation of european citizens of african descent by taking the opportunity to highlight the specific form of social exclusion they face. in this introductory speech, it is my task to explain to the president of our assembly, to the members of the commission to which the question is addressed, to the members present groups. of course, there has been controversy. official recognition of the specific history of afro-descendants, the possibility of instituting reparations, the issue of public apologies, but also discussion in committee, and we can be quite satisfied with the final version of the resolution, the result of serious and competent mediation. it is now necessary to return to the general importance of the question, to reaffirm some of the principles which have led us to treat it. the equal social integration of european citizens of african descent must, in my view, be framed within the requirements of respect for fundamental human rights. the whole point is to guarantee to those who bear diversity the integrity of the human dignity of which they are the undisputed holders. these statements, which start at the very foundations of our political thinking, are motivated by the fact that in europe today, despite centuries of theorizing about rationality and social evolution, there are still values that undermine the lives of people of african descent. often it is said in the middle because it seems unthinkable: however, a specific study by the european agency for fundamental rights has given us evidence of the existence, within european society, of recurrent phenomena of anti-black racism. in addition, in several member states, the daily news is often dominated by incidents of racism and xenophobia, which affect european citizens of african descent indifferently and tend to push them to the margins of society. the scale of the phenomenon is such that no sector of society can be considered immune. the rights to housing, access to decent work and the right to education appear to be particularly violated. in some european countries we have even seen the attempted return of apartheid, with the discriminatory exclusion of children of african descent from school canteens and the attempt to set up separate classes for them. when i referred to the debates in the libe committee, i referred to the question of the historical relations between the european countries, now members of the union, and the african countries, the ultimate place of origin of afro-europeans. this historical relationship has seen, among other things, the post-medieval explorations, the black slave trade, colonization, the total economic exploitation of africa and the thinly veiled forms of neo-colonialism that are in force in our times. the question of migration, which is an essential part of globalisation, has often been the subject of intense debate in this house and in our societies, and has also sharpened our differences of opinion. i believe that the question of full citizenship for black europeans of african descent must be included in this complex of issues, in order to understand its depth, but also to be able to remedy it. often, even among ourselves, i have seen some of our colleagues surprised to hear me say that racism exists in europe, thinking it government... mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the special committee on financial crimes, tax evasion and tax avoidance has delivered its final report without compromise: europe has a serious problem of money laundering and tax fraud. the eu member states have not done enough to close the gaps in tax rules: in fact, many governments have shown a lack of will to tackle tax evasion and financial crime, blocking legislation aimed at a common tax base and digital levying. the european commission itself has avoided proposing a reform that would have ended the veto power of governments in tax matters, so that seven member states, luxembourg, belgium, cyprus, hungary, ireland, malta and the netherlands, are de facto acting as tax havens and this is a situation that cannot last any longer. europol has too limited powers: the commission is currently coordinating the work of national forces, when they are willing to cooperate. a european financial police force with investigative powers is needed.
in writing. tax evasion, tax avoidance and financial crime have serious consequences for the european budget, unduly draining resources intended to provide services to citizens. moreover, financial crime and money laundering, in addition to depriving states of tax revenues, distort fair competition between businesses and are sometimes exploited by terrorist networks and organised crime groups to fund their illicit activities. i therefore believe that in order to counter these serious threats, member states must further strengthen the exchange of information between national authorities, as well as give full effect to the existing european anti-money laundering directives. in fact, today, technological developments facilitate the mobility of capital by allowing large sums of money to be moved from one country to another in a very short time. i therefore believe that it is essential to strengthen cooperation between national fius and law enforcement authorities by setting up a european fiu to coordinate the flow of information. with a view to strengthening supervision at european level, i also believe that the powers of the european banking authority (eba) should be extended in the fight against money laundering, and that a genuine financial police with investigative powers should be set up within europol.
the european parliament has been a very active participant in the debate on the future of the european union. the resolution we are discussing is one of many contributions by parliament to this subject. the monitoring, however, presupposes that our role is neutral, never electoral, careful to avoid double standards and punitive attitudes, and that the aim is to strengthen national antibodies, without pretending to replace them totally, presuppositions which i do not think are entirely satisfied in the resolution. i'm not asking you to abdicate our role, but to make it unimpeachable. otherwise, the risk is that the european institutions will increasingly be seen as an orwellian power and the rule of law will be perceived as an external imposition to be resisted.

and this can be due to a dramatic event, a climatic event, a terrorist event, a particular overload, a breakdown - the member states are left to themselves and to the good hearted - i would like to hear this expression - of the neighbouring countries, where interconnections allow it. the dynamics, as demonstrated by the crisis in winter 2017 in south-east europe, affects european citizens by impacting on the availability of services, energy prices, household financial equilibrium and industrial production. the question was, and is, how to facilitate - in the context of an energy crisis - the movement of energy under certain conditions to where it is most needed in the union, regardless of national political boundaries. as a parliament, we therefore had a task above all others, namely to ensure that the criteria for mutual cooperation in the event of an energy crisis were sufficiently stringent, both in terms of the methodologies for assessing scenarios between countries, and therefore the principle of interoperability, and in terms of the criteria for mutual assistance. i must acknowledge the determination of the council in defending its demands, without however neglecting its readiness to dialogue towards compromise, and the commission's very valuable mediation work at some decisive stages of the negotiations, without whose contribution we would not have reached a framework agreement so quickly. the text for the vote in this house is therefore in the direction desired by parliament. the methodologies for defining country-specific crisis scenarios and subsequently for crisis intervention should be homogeneous, drawn up in accordance with a single model and free from bias by non-institutional market players. the principle of mutual assistance is reaffirmed in even stricter terms, by specifying that the only element of the mutual assistance obligations of the member states is to be recognised only if the infrastructure is not in place and the interconnections permit it. the member states have a duty to assist each other. more detailed guidelines are also provided for the definition of compensation criteria, the nature of which is however left to the discretion of the respective national authorities. we ran the risk that this negotiation would become the instrument for changing the balance in the negotiations on the other files in the package, a danger of which we were - and i was - well aware but which i believe we have overcome, also thanks to the fruitful cooperation with the other rapporteurs. i would like to thank very much president busek, who has given a wise coordination in the negotiations, the shadow rapporteurs for a really excellent cooperation at all stages of this dossier, and commissioner cañete, who has worked with us very well.

italy, which had either failed to impose fines on car manufacturers for breaking european union rules or did not fully implement international legislative sanctions on car manufacturers breaking european union emission rules. in 2017 and 2018, the commission sent complementary letters of formal notice to germany, luxembourg, spain and the uk to request further information. a letter of formal notice was also sent to italy regarding the emission control strategy used by fiat 500x euro 6 diesel model. the information received from the member states so far is neither fully satisfactory nor complete, and in addition, new cases of emission irregularities are being reported. the commission will continue to follow up these cases. some of you also have referred to the recalls. our recall information platform was launched on 6 february 2018, and almost all member states are regularly updating the information on mandatory and voluntary recalls and the results of this platform are public. today, only eight member states have issued a mandatory recall for vehicles of the vw group with illegal defeat devices. those are austria, denmark, finland, france, germany, netherlands, portugal and slovenia. in the european union, the wide recall rate of the affected vw models, equipped with the ea189 engine, is at 80% as of 18 march 2019. unfortunately, in some member states, there are still recall rates below 50%. our overall objective is to reach a 100% recall rate and as our first step, as announced in craiova (romania) in the roadmap towards clean vehicles, a minimum european union-wide recall rate of 90% should be reached by the end of 2019. you can be sure that the commission is committed to making sure that we get to the bottom of dieselgate. the member states and industry must take all measures still necessary in order to be able to close the dieselgate chapter. we will continue working on the implementing rules for the type-approval framework. we will market surveillance rules in place. but it has to be stressed that implementation and enforcement is primarily the responsibility of the member states themselves, as is the recalling of non-compliant on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, e-commerce needs the confidence of consumers to grow, who need to feel protected when buying online as well as in traditional shops, whether they are buying physical or digital goods. these two directives improve the existing protection and make it more accessible to consumers. we also do not add onerous tasks for vendors, especially if they are smes and micro-enterprises. thus, if a defect of conformity is found, the buyer can ask the seller to repair or replace the goods and then have the right to a price reduction or to terminate the contract. on this front, however, we must also strengthen the protection of small retailers and smes vis-à-vis producers. indeed, the costs incurred by the dealers for the repair or replacement may be very onerous and disproportionate to the profits. in addition, in terms of protection, it is now written in black and white that those who buy a digital good will have the same protections as those who buy a physical good. so if you buy music or movies online, you'll have the same protections as if you bought a cd or dvd. for example, if the download fails or the service is of poor quality, you will be entitled to replacement and refund, and this with a future-proof approach, because it will also apply to social media, video and audio sharing platforms and instant messaging services. this is an important result because consumers must have the highest possible level of protection, whatever technology they use.

president-in-office of the council. – mr president, it’s a pleasure for me to participate today in this debate on the implementation of the eu budget for the financial year 2017, in the context of the annual discharge procedure, as foreseen in article 319 of the treaty. the council attaches great importance to the discharge exercise. it is important that eu funds are used according to the rules and that expenditure respects the principles of sound financial management. on 20 february, my colleague ms luminița odobescu, the permanent representative of romania to the european union, had the honour of presenting to the committee on budgetary control (cont) the council’s recommendation to grant discharge to the commission. this plenary will hold a vote today and, i believe, will confirm the vote of the committee on budgetary control and grant discharge to the commission. on the one hand, the council welcomes the fact that, for the second time in a row, the court gives a qualified opinion on the legality and regularity of payments. additionally, the council welcomes the gradual reduction of the overall estimated level of error, as reported by the court over the last years. on the other hand, the council regrets that the overall estimated level of error for 2017 payments – at 2.4 % – is still above the benchmark of 2 %. the council, therefore, reiterates its wish to see further improvements in the financial management systems and in the estimated level of errors across all policy areas. the year 2017 was a special one, not only because it sits in the middle of the period covered by the multiannual financial framework, but also because of the changes in the control and assurance framework. this was particularly important in the area of cohesion, where the court has introduced a new approach: for the first time, it checked assurance packages submitted by member states for the current programming period. having that in mind, a sustained improvement has been observed in the management of the eu budget over the past few years. the overall error rate for payments decreased in 2017 for the fourth year in a row. the member states and the commission have been able to improve their management and their control systems. this good work has to be kept up. there is, of course, room for improvement, especially in reimbursement—based payments, which still account for the highest proportion of errors. the rules are still very complicated, both for beneficiaries to follow and for authorities to check. a simpler, more transparent and more predictable regulatory framework is essential to ensure the effective and correct management of eu funds. in the same approach, the council takes note of the court’s recommendation concerning the simplification and streamlining of the strategic frameworks that govern the implementation of the eu budget. this is also about making sure that the budget delivers results connected to the objectives of the union. european taxpayers must see that their money is not wasted and, furthermore, is spent on what matters to them and makes a difference. this is why the council supports the court’s recommendation to streamline indicators on the performance of the eu budget and to improve the alignment between high-level general objectives and specific programme and policy objectives, thereby reinforcing accountability for results and increasing clarity and transparency for all stakeholders. increasing focus on performance measurement, however, should not prevent the court from continuing its essential work on the annual reports and providing the estimated level of error for all spending areas both in the current and in the next multiannual financial framework. this is particularly important in headings 3 (security and citizenship) and 4 (global europe), where expenditure is of increasing political significance. going back to the way the budget and the finances of the eu are managed, the council found some important elements of concern. there is a significant level of outstanding budgetary commitments and the budget is also exposed to contingent liabilities. the council would like the commission to improve the payment estimates and to follow the court’s recommendation to provide more information about the situation of liabilities and about the use of financial instruments. this is an absolute must to ensure the transparency and predictability of eu funding. the european parliament and the council seem, in general, to share the same approach. we welcome the improvements that are there for all to see, and we want to see the good work of member states’ authorities, of the commission and of the court, sustained and further improved. we have to send a clear signal to european citizens and taxpayers that eu funds are used in a responsible and accountable manner.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow we are going to vote on the new instrument for neighbourhood, development and international cooperation. this is a very important procedure as it will determine how the european union's assistance to third countries will be extended over the period 2021-2027. this is a value of almost 90 billion euros. the text is the result of a long process of negotiation and compromise between all the political groups; we have reached a position which i consider to be balanced on the merger of the various existing financial instruments, so as to ensure greater direction and control by the european parliament. that is the first point i think it is necessary to stress, namely governance. the commission proposal only provides for implementing acts and comitology for the adoption of programming documents: this means that parliament can only challenge these acts on legal grounds, i.e. if the commission has exceeded its implementing powers, and not on the basis of the political decisions which gave rise to them. this is clearly not enough and we are therefore introducing delegated acts, a more meaningful and regular strategic dialogue that precedes the programming decisions. in this way, therefore, all important policy choices would be subject to parliament's scrutiny and objection. a second element is the neighbourhood policy, which is one of the priority areas and a key element of the european union's external action. including the neighbourhood policy in the single instrument provides greater flexibility for easy and rapid mobilisation of additional funding and to support special relations with our neighbours. the budget foreseen of eur 22 billion represents an increase of 24% in this sector compared with the current multiannual financial framework. as far as sub-saharan africa is concerned, we are increasing its financial allocation and are planning a programme for the acp countries so that they can meet the possible needs arising from a future post-cotonou agreement. we have included in the objectives of the regulation a reference to the eradication of poverty and, as regards official development aid, we have increased the percentage of projects financed meeting these criteria from 92 to 95%. on migration, we stress the need for a holistic and long-term approach and address the root causes of regular, irregular and forced migration, including a reference to climate refugees. so let's talk about the need for human rights-based policies to facilitate safe, orderly and regular migration. we also consider it important to tackle climate change, also in relation to the agreements reached, including the paris agreement, and the percentage of expenditure on climate change has been increased to 45% in the regulation objectives, an ambitious target compared to the one proposed by the commission. the priority is the intervention we make in the field of human rights. we have introduced a clause to suspend aid to a particular country in the event of persistent non-compliance with these principles. finally, as regards the part of the instrument dealing with peace and stability, we would like to emphasize clearly that the funds in this area must be used to create conditions for ensuring sustainable development and cannot be used for the purchase of arms and ammunition or for operations with military or defence implications. it is important work that has taken many months and for this reason i naturally thank all three of my co-rapporteurs and the undersigned for the work the agenda includes the report by mr brando benifei, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, on 'after the arab spring: future prospects for the middle east and north africa' (2018/2160(ini)) (a8-0077/2019)
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, eight years ago thousands of women and men, especially young people, took to the streets across the southern and eastern shores of the mediterranean to demand more democracy, respect for their rights, fundamental freedoms, work and social inclusion. eight years after those protests, which marked a break with the patterns of the past, it is time to take stock of the transformations that have taken place in the region and especially of the action of the european union. while what is commonly called the 'arab spring', which was in fact a series of stages, led individual countries to take different paths, from greater democratization to new regimes, if not to a situation of civil war, europe first tried to accompany the democratic impulses that had emerged. however, following the growing terrorist threat of daesh and the outbreak of the refugee crisis, europe has been led to focus more on stabilising our partner countries, security and immigration containment. in short, we have once again repeated the mistakes of the past, not realizing that this would continue the vicious circle from which the people of this complicated region are trying to break free. we are still witnessing this today in algeria, which risks becoming a new syria if the situation is underestimated once again. the union would have many means at its disposal for a more effective foreign policy, but a renewed action must necessarily start from a coordinated approach and greater unity. if the member states continue to pursue their own interests in a very short-term perspective, sometimes in conflict with each other, we will continue to be unable to influence the complex processes that are going on in the region, and will therefore increasingly play the role of payers and not actors, as has happened in syria. we must therefore rethink our policy towards this important part of our neighbourhood, taking up our basic principles as the north star. as outlined in the global strategy for the common foreign and security policy, we need to invest more in the resilience of these societies rather than in mere stabilisation: the european union is a major player in the world economy, and its role in the world economy is increasingly recognised. instead, a long-term approach is needed, focusing on people and their aspirations, democracy, human rights, social inclusion and socioeconomic development. in the end, what has emerged from the arab spring is first and foremost a major crisis of confidence on the part of citizens in their institutions, which requires the construction of a new social contract, which the union must encourage and support. the report therefore proposes an approach which takes account of the views of the populations concerned: a constant and structured dialogue with civil society, including its smaller and local components; an approach that gives a strong voice to young people, who are an important and dynamic but also vulnerable part of these societies. we therefore propose the establishment of permanent advisory councils for young people in the union's delegations and a programme of study and work exchange on the model of erasmus euro-mediterranean, with dedicated resources. we also call, among the many points raised, on the member states to put an end to the sale of arms and equipment used for internal repression against regimes which do not respect human rights. we also stress that greater cooperation cannot be separated from investigative and judicial cooperation, even in cases involving young europeans, such as the notorious case of giulio regeni, for which we are still awaiting the truth. we therefore need, in conclusion, a paradigm shift and we believe that this report points the way towards a path which is more in line with the aspirations of dialogue, growth and cooperation with our southern and mediterranean neighbours.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the young people who have taken to the streets all over the world in recent weeks have asked us to act urgently, to do something quickly for sustainable development. europe is taking action and is making another point in favour of the environment and the fight against plastic pollution, especially in our seas, not only in the oceans but also in the mediterranean sea, where entire islands of waste have been created. with this new directive we are banning single-use plastic products such as cotton wool, dishes and cutlery, which are among the main causes of marine pollution, for which there are already alternatives available on the market, which are recyclable and have the potential to last longer. at the same time, we are also encouraging the use of recycled plastic in products, by setting a minimum content for, for example, beverage bottles. in short, today we are taking an important step forward in the transition to a circular economy, which we in europe have understood firsthand and immediately, and the importance of maintaining a high level of growth and well-being for our citizens, protecting the environment and remaining competitive in the world. it's going to be a long process, because we're going to have to change our patterns of production and consumption, but i think that's the only way forward.

the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. in particular, at a time when the economic and social effects of the long crisis we are experiencing have not yet been fully felt, it is very appropriate to put in place all possible legal means to enable companies to embark on restructuring measures, which will allow them to save economic activity first and then be helped by formal measures of insolvency and then liquidation, thus trying to avoid the loss of jobs and, with it, the dramatic social consequences which this often entails. the text we are about to vote on is the result of long negotiations involving parliament first and parliament and the council second. but for this reason, which has enabled us to deal with the most sensitive points, as my colleagues have pointed out previously, we cannot regard it as negative. we must not, however, hide the fact that we have lost an important opportunity, in our view, to ensure strong protection for the most vulnerable in this dramatic phase, in some areas, of business restructuring, which has involved the large european companies but, very often, also the weakest, medium and small ones. a restructuring plan normally does not concern only financial issues, which are the most obvious in many circumstances, but restructuring inevitably extends to issues concerning the organization of the company, not only because the organization, when it is deficient, produces difficulties but also because to get out of these difficulties it is necessary to change the organizational model that is the cause of the crisis. the process therefore also concerns the remuneration of workers and employment conditions, meaning by conditions both the number of people involved and the extent and character, including cultural, of the work that is lost in many circumstances. we have therefore worked to recognise and formalise the need for the preventive involvement and full information of workers, as well as all other actors and stakeholders who are in contact with the company. we have indeed made considerable progress in this respect, as has been said, and for this we must thank, and i do so gladly, the rapporteur's efforts, especially during the very long trilogue. it would have been appropriate to add a few more steps, however, and it is particularly important to include the obligation to confirm workers for all those elements of the plan which concern the organizational aspects of the enterprise, including, of course, dismissals, economic conditions, working hours and material conditions. the absence of this point represents for us one of those missed opportunities for good legislation and real progress for the weakest. another point on which i think we have missed an opportunity concerns, again, the workers. this time, however, not as a workforce, but as part of the company's organization, but as possible creditors of a company in crisis. we believe that creditors cannot all be treated equally and that it would be useful and necessary to provide greater protection for the weakest creditors, namely the workers. in particular, we believe that the provision of a specific class for claims of employees cannot be a matter for the member states but should be mandatory. furthermore, it would have been appropriate to grant preferential rights and additional protections to this class in comparison with all other classes. we 'll stop here . we are satisfied with what has been achieved, but we hope that this directive will be adopted tomorrow, but we anticipate what we think and we will therefore continue to work so that what has been a missed opportunity today will be, in the future and above all for the new parliament which will be elected by the european citizens in the coming weeks, an opportunity to return to the subject and to ensure real progress for the benefit of all, both the company and the workforce.

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice president of the commission / high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – mr president, let me first welcome, on behalf of the high representative, your broad support for her proposal to establish a european peace facility. this reflects the need, repeatedly emphasised by this house, for funding in this area that is more flexible and efficient and which better embodies solidarity. let me extend, on behalf of the high representative and other colleagues, our thanks to the rapporteur, ms vautmans, as well as the co-rapporteurs, for their engagement and their constructive and pragmatic approach. as you rightly recall in your report, the union’s ambition is to be a global security provider, something which is obviously in our collective strategic interest. given the growing and evolving threat picture which we face, we need to have the capacity to respond to a variety of security challenges. that was clearly acknowledged in the global strategy in 2016. the idea of the peace facility was born out of our experience, as the rapporteur was just setting out. the eu is active on the ground, but there are strong limitations to what we can achieve currently. for example, we’ve had difficulties in financing the training of soldiers in somalia and we have not always been able to provide the central african republic with the equipment it needs, as was recalled, to complete its transformation from civil war to a functioning modern democracy. the cost of eu military operations fall too much on the countries which are contributing troops, and that acts as a deterrent to others when it comes to participation and deployments. this new facility, when adopted by the council, will make a real difference. it will provide the union with the ability to finance all operational actions under the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) with military or defence implications in a flexible, responsive manner. in particular there are three main strands of action that the peace facility will support. first, it will cover the common costs of eu military missions and operations. indeed, more costs should be funded in common to better meet operational needs and to facilitate deployments. second, it will enable the eu to contribute to military peace operations led by other international actors. and third, it will allow the eu to support the armed forces of our partner countries with infrastructure, equipment or military assistance when the council so decides. the nature, scope and limits of these actions will be defined by the council, but the proposal makes very clear that any support to our partners would be subject to strict controls such as respect for democratic principles and fundamental rights. the high representative’s proposal benefits from the support of the commission, in accordance with article 31. this support will help to facilitate synergies with our other financial instruments and to underpin sound financial management. in conclusion, let me underline that this is a key part of the work that we’re doing collectively to make our citizens more secure, to better support our partners around the world and to contribute to our most precious common good, which is, of course, peace and security. so let me thank you again for your support for this important initiative. i look forward to our discussion and support tomorrow.
the instrument for financing european military operations is a further step towards ever closer cooperation between the member states in the field of the common security and defence policy, as well as a mechanism to rationalise existing mechanisms. as a parliament we make a significant contribution to the high representative's proposal, first and foremost, the clear requirement that military actions financed through this instrument be in accordance with the principles and values enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights and international law. we also call for strict control by parliament itself, which must be kept informed and have access to all the documents relating to operations financed under the instrument. the transfer or sale of military equipment or materiel to third countries must be in accordance with the eu's common position on arms export controls and the dual-use control regime, while a detailed list of supplied materials must also be made available, safeguards necessary because security and defence policy cannot be without coherence with the values of peace and respect for human rights, which are at the heart of the european project. i am also particularly pleased that, on my proposal, reference has been made to non-proliferation and disarmament and to the european union's leading role in the fight to ban nuclear weapons. in times of increasing uncertainty, when only a few civil society organisations seem to be genuinely committed to these objectives, the nuclear threat is no longer a ghost of the past but a real danger, to be actively combated through international law and multilateralism, of which the union is a world leader.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the growing political instability in many parts of the world, from russia to ukraine, north africa and the middle east, is forcing europe to act to overcome the critical problems of our continent's supply system. a genuine common energy policy will reduce costs for citizens and businesses, while at the same time the use of renewable energy sources will be an important input in ensuring the competitiveness of entire energy-intensive sectors. we must continue on the path started with the legislative packages for reforming the energy and gas markets and support the necessary establishment of connecting infrastructure, including alternative ones, which guarantee security of supply. the european effort should concentrate on reducing internal barriers, as my colleague mr zorrinho said, along with building up sufficient storage capacity to cope with moments of crisis. this agreement ensures - and it is important - that all gas pipelines, including offshore pipelines with third countries, are subject to the principles of european law, and the derogation scheme envisaged protects existing investments - i think in southern europe - in view of the future reform of the internal gas market.
on behalf of the green group in the european parliament. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the social and economic value of the fisheries sector is not in question. i think that in all the long discussions we have had in the last few months on this matter, this has never been brought into question. the difference is how we ensure the economic and social value of this sector. we believe that the way to ensure this, and to make it safe, to maintain it over time, is to ensure that the resource that keeps this sector going is kept healthy, and then of course to keep the ecosystems and fish stocks that underpin the fishing industry healthy. we therefore believe that the emff should first of all help to achieve the objectives of the common fisheries policy. the common fisheries policy has been in place for six years now and has largely failed to achieve its objectives and is failing to do so. there are also elements in the text, in my view, in our view, which suggest that we can still increase fishing capacity at a time when, as we know, in the north-east of our seas we have over 40% of overfished fish stocks and in the mediterranean, unfortunately - we will talk about this later - well over 80%. we have managed to limit the budget for research, for data collection, for the protection of ecosystems, for the protection of biodiversity, but we have asked and were asking, at least we greens, for something much more significant and important, such as 25%. we got 10 percent, which is good, but it's not great, definitely. other points have been inserted which we do not like, and the plant in which this emff has been built does not like us, and for that reason we will vote against it.
on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, until now, amidst restrictions and red tape, the majority of small fishermen have not received a penny from the emff. today the regulation accepts our proposals based on simplification and an increase in the budget to 7.7 billion. simplifying means keeping in mind that the emff must be first and foremost a fund for fishermen. that means giving importance, yes, to environmental priorities, but when there is a reduction in fishing effort, that is where the funds must act. so it is right to reintroduce temporary detention support, the possibility of modernising vessels, regardless of the age of the beneficiary, and above all a clear rule specifying in detail the conditions and duration of the period of ineligibility according to the types of infringement, because it is absurd to punish fishermen for ridiculous infringements. we will finally be funding the protection of safety at sea and the health of workers. fishermen will have access to financial and insurance instruments in the event of accidents at sea and natural disasters, and to compensation for damage caused by protected marine birds and mammals, through simplified procedures and in advance.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, despite all our good intentions, fishing is unfortunately one of the subjects on which the european union is most often called to account. of course, many times wrong, but often right too, if we put ourselves in the shoes of our fishermen. the powerful report by mr mato has addressed the many problems of the sector, but much remains to be done, particularly in the mediterranean, in small-scale fishing and in the simplification of complex rules which are increasingly becoming insurmountable barriers for those who make a living from fishing. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. the european union's financial support must be stepped up in this respect, otherwise we will only be favouring cartels, we will be abolishing small-scale fishing and we will be increasing the sense of hostility towards the union that is more than ever at this time.
on behalf of the green group in the european parliament. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i do not agree with the rapporteur when she says that since this is the first mediterranean plan, any plan is more or less acceptable. in fact, precisely because the mediterranean is in the situation we know and which we have all stressed, we would need a much, much stronger plan. i would remind you that among the species covered by this plan, there are some that, according to the researchers, according to the science, are being fished four or five times over the level of maximum sustainable yield. this msy is not a definition, it's not a word. it means what stocks can give us, year by year, so that they can be maintained over time. right on msy here we have the admission of a major failure: we're going to get a year away from what should be the limit to achieve this goal and say we can't do it, we can't do it and we're going to push it back another five years. a serious and clear failure. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware of the fact that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. i would prefer this weak, ineffective plan to the status quo. it is better to start from something, better to create at least a starting point and hope that this can somehow serve as an incentive in the future to try to do much, much better. that is why, although we have tried in every way to discuss this work again and even to send it back to committee before it goes to the trilogue, we are not satisfied with the way it has turned out, but that is precisely why we will vote in favour, because we are satisfied in some way and we hope that it is a first step towards something much more important in the future.
on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this multiannual plan contains measures for the protection of species of biological and commercial interest, but balanced with economic and social aspects for the survival of thousands of fishing companies. the rules of procedure accept many of our amendments: we have eliminated the introduction of fishing quotas, the effort management regime will have a reduction of up to 40% over a period of five years. there will be derogations from the use of trawls, depending on the specific characteristics of our coasts and our fishing techniques. a one-size-fits-all rule would have put us at a huge disadvantage. our seabed is diverse, and our fishing has always adapted to geographical characteristics without affecting biodiversity. until now, the european union has not taken account of the characteristics of fleets in terms of navigation and technical equipment. today, however, the months of closure will be chosen by the states according to regionalisation. this is the first plan to allow the use of the emff to finance fishermen who opt for permanent cessation. the negotiations were long and arduous, and we are not entirely satisfied, but we have improved the text considerably and have given voice to the main demands of small-scale fisheries.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to congratulate mrs clara aguilera garcía on her work and on the fact that she has taken the specific features of the western mediterranean into account in the proposal for a multiannual management plan. the proposal includes measures to improve the conservation of resources and the environmental sustainability of stocks. however, in order to achieve social and economic sustainability alongside environmental sustainability, it is necessary to approve the proposed changes to achieve a balance and reduce the impact on the territories. in addition to temporary cessation measures, member states should be allowed to introduce compensatory measures for the permanent cessation of fishing vessels affected by the fishing effort reduction measures proposed in the plan. the right flexibility is needed in the ban on trawling. the local fleets have adapted to the characteristics of their fishing grounds. an excessive reduction of these areas based solely on geographical or topographical criteria could therefore cause irreversible socioeconomic damage to the sector. cooperation with third countries with which stocks are shared should be developed within the framework of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, in order to ensure efficient management of fisheries activities and the effectiveness of regional management plans.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, as you all know, in february this year the european commission proposed a revision of directive 2008/96/ec on the safety management of road infrastructure, for which i have happily taken on the role of rapporteur, especially considering that this is a matter of particular concern to me, as a member of parliament and as a mother. and that is exactly the point of view i intend to start with. according to a survey carried out by ansa europe, over 8 000 children have died in serious road accidents in the last ten years. this is a huge number which saddens me immensely and which is part of a much larger picture, which is made up of over 25 000 deaths per year in the union. this directive sets out a whole series of specific objectives to try to reduce these important figures as much as possible, in the spirit of improving road safety in the union, including through better management by the member states, making the enforcement of legislation more effective in order to achieve the objective of zero fatalities in the european union by 2050, the so-called 'vision zero', as proposed by the commission. this review is intended to be one of the focal points for achieving this objective, together with other elements such as improving the interaction of the main european infrastructures with technologically interconnected means and protecting vulnerable users. in essence, we are talking about a very important legislative proposal which has several elements, all of them essential, on which i am very proud to have been able to work with the council, which i would like to thank again for the spirit of cooperation shown during the negotiations. the main thing to remember and always keep in mind is that the previous directive applied only to roads which are part of the ten-t network, whether they are in the planning, design, construction or already open to traffic. on the contrary, the new revision takes into account all motorways and primary roads, not just those forming part of the ten-t network, and this will lead to a drastic reduction in road accidents resulting in fatalities or serious injuries. many of the initiatives proposed by this directive refer to the technological progress in mobility that we are about to experience at this very historic moment, especially with regard to the new generation of cars equipped with increasingly advanced driver assistance systems. so let us remember that to support this and to promote the prevention needed to drastically reduce accidents, we need to work towards having ever smarter and more interconnected roads with these vehicles. for example, member states will have to pay particular attention to the legibility and recognition of signage, both for drivers and for automated driving assistance systems. all this on the basis of common specifications at european level. since it is our duty in this parliament to protect all citizens, we have also made sure that the needs of vulnerable road users - i am talking about pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists - must be taken into account in the member states when implementing the procedures set out in the directive. in the same spirit, we have also provided the opportunity for citizens to submit voluntary reports on the problems they identify at the road level, thus facilitating the interaction between the infrastructure itself and those who use it. finally, we can say that another fundamental step has been taken towards improving road user safety, although i am always aware that this directive is only a piece of a larger picture, which includes prevention and a different safety culture. i am confident that this path will lead to the expected results in the designated time, avoiding that individuals or families suffer the loss of loved ones due to road accidents, events that are both tragic and avoidable if addressed in advance and in the most correct way.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in 2017, more than 25 000 people died on european roads, and the death rate has remained stable for some years, despite some member states continuing to make progress on safety. paradoxically, less than 10% of fatal road accidents occur on motorways, compared with 37% in urban areas and 55% on country roads. the advantage of a road infrastructure safety management directive is the convergence towards higher standards of infrastructure safety across the union. the application of community rules on infrastructure safety should be extended to all major roads in europe. the most stringent rules, which apply only to major motorways and the transeuropean road network, must also be respected in urban and rural areas. the commission's goal of zero fatalities by 2050 cannot be achieved without the help of technology, making driver assistance and safety systems mandatory, and direct help to member states to pinpoint the most dangerous roads and make them safer. i congratulate the rapporteur.

in writing. in order to achieve the goal of 'zero fatalities' by 2050, i welcome the commission's request to amend directive 2008/96/ec on road safety and infrastructure management. the approval of the text will extend the application of the provision to all motorways, including primary roads and those outside the ten-t network. the main innovation is the possibility of making a concrete assessment of road conditions at the network level, taking into account both the safety measures present or visually detectable and a set of other data, which can be deduced from the incidence of accidents occurring on the network, their severity and the need for inspections to resolve sensitive and dangerous situations. another important new feature is the provision for common specific provisions for vertical and horizontal signs, which allow for easy readability and recognition in connection with driver assistance devices installed on vehicles. we will finally have useful and reliable data that will allow us to identify the so-called "death trails". through constant traffic monitoring, we can precisely improve those roads and highways that are not safe.

member of the commission. – mr president, thank you for this debate. i’m just going to respond on two points, if that’s alright. first of all there have been a number of suggestions, particularly from behind me, that in some way the work that we’re doing to tackle disinformation is against free speech, that in some way it amounts to censorship. i want to be absolutely clear about this. we have never suggested, we will not suggest, that it is the responsibility of someone, whether it is public authorities, still less private sector, to judge whether a piece of political speech or a piece of political information is true or false, good or bad. the measures that we are seeking to promote through the code are measures to promote greater transparency around political debate and political speech, greater transparency around the provenance of particular pieces of information – where does it come from? – so that we as citizens can be better equipped to assess that information and form our own judgments about it. that’s what is involved in the measures that we are promoting through the code, to have greater transparency around political adverts, sponsored content, to tackle the problems of bots and fake accounts, to use fact checkers more effectively, to have that independent scrutiny that many of you have spoken about, so that we know what is happening on these social media platforms, to have effective corrections when some piece of demonstrable disinformation has been circulated. for me, that’s the essence of defending free speech and free debate, and it is as far away as you can be from any sense of censorship. the second thing that i want to react to: the importance of our cyber resilience, protecting ourselves from cyber-attacks, cyber-enabled interference. this compliant products and fair competition in the single market reach final consumers. every day we encounter dangerous, illegal, counterfeit products, in increasing numbers and affecting mainly sectors with a strong impact on daily life. 32% of toys, 58% of electronic devices and 47% of construction products do not meet the safety or consumer information requirements laid down by law. in addition, should be greater cooperation at political and operational level between the authorities of the member states, in order to build common strategies and ensure a uniform and consistent system of controls. in particular, we want to eliminate 'port shopping', i.e. the existence of entry points favoured by dishonest traders because of the less rigid or sometimes total absence of customs controls. we have therefore set out harmonised objectives and standards for border controls, common risk methodologies, and increased coordination and mutual assistance between national authorities at the level of the european network. we also demanded a system of supervision, where there is no longer any room for conflicts of interest between the controller and the controlled, or for preferential treatment for the operators who are not in compliance. we have therefore supported the european commission's proposal to set up a network of public laboratories in the european union, which can increase the monitoring capacity of individual member states, based on specific competences and shared priorities. finally, we have increased the powers available to national authorities to carry out effective investigations and controls, including in the web world, with regard to the most technologically sophisticated products. these are the main results achieved. i hope there will be a broad consensus on this proposal.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, you have heard the rapporteur list the percentages for products which are still unsafe. they're impressive, they're worrying. think about 32 percent of toys, they're for children, mostly, and 40 percent of personal protective equipment, they're for our bodies. in the face of this situation, with the growth of electronic commerce, it is inevitable that there will be greater risks and it is equally necessary that the steps forward that we have tried to put together, with a result as important and positive as the one we are discussing, be taken. now, it is also important to define an economic operator who ensures compliance of all products. i am therefore very pleased that the commission has taken this initiative. in the previous legislature, parliament had voted on a very ambitious text on product safety, which had been blocked in the council because of opposition to the introduction of the 'made in' rules. too bad we could have gotten to this point sooner. in any case, let us look at what has been done and it will now be up to the future commission to make practical in all the countries what we are positively discussing and approving, i imagine, tomorrow.

member of the commission. – mr president, i welcome the agreement on this important file. i would like once again to praise our rapporteur, mr lópez aguilar, and of course the shadow rapporteurs, for their work on this new legislation. the tourism and travel industry plays, as we all know, a key role in the european economy, and not only representing around 10% of the european union’s gdp. lengthy and cumbersome procedures can deter tourists from travelling to europe. this would deprive us of investment and spending and affect in a negative way the european union’s economy. the agreed changes will make it easier for millions of travellers to obtain a visa to come to the european union every year, facilitating tourism, trade and business. making the process easier will not mean a free pass to the european union or more lax security checks. the new rules will actually improve and strengthen our security standards to detect those who pose a threat or have no right to enter the european union. a new mechanism in our visa code will enable us to use the leverage of our visa policy, in cooperation with non-eu countries, when it comes to the return and readmission of irregular migrants. the new rules include procedures that are more flexible for travellers coming to the schengen area. why? according to the current rules, the earliest date one can file an application is three months prior to their trip. the new rules extend this period to six months. the equal treatment of applicants will also be ensured. frequent travellers with a positive visa history can receive a multiple entry visa, with a gradually-increasing validity period from one year to a maximum of five years. this will save time and decrease costs both for applicants and member states. at the same time, the fulfilment of entry conditions by the travellers will be thoroughly and repeatedly verified in all cases. a moderate increase of the schengen visa fee from eur 60 to eur 80 is also suggested in order to secure additional resources for strengthening security. this modest increase will allow member states to maintain adequate levels of consular staff worldwide. this will ensure stronger security screenings as well as the upgrading of id equipment and software without representing an obstacle for the visa applicants. to sum it all up, the new eu visa code will adapt the rules to evolving draft report by the committee on transport and tourism. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank the commissioner for his words and i thank you and all your collaborators and staff. on the subject of today's debate, i welcome the developments in this revision of the visa code to facilitate mobility, such as the possibility of submitting applications up to six months before a planned stay; reduced fare options for young people; facilitating multiple-entry visas for frequent travellers and specific recognition for cultural professionals and athletes. it is regrettable that the opportunity was not taken to address the outdated regulatory restriction which prevents legitimate travellers from staying longer in the schengen area without exceeding the legal thresholds in individual member states. the european parliament has twice shown support for these longer stays and the current 90 days with a 180 day limitation were conceived when the schengen area was smaller.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the tourism industry is very important for the economic development of the european union. in 2018, it brought in more than €700 billion to europe, has more than 2 million businesses employing more than 12 million people. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation. these figures speak for themselves. the tourism industry is growing and it is important to facilitate those with a legitimate interest in travelling to europe. this reform is the right step in this direction, simplifying the regulatory framework, reducing the time needed and adapting the visa procedures to new technologies. i am confident that this reform will also serve to improve cooperation with third countries to facilitate the return of their own citizens who are in europe illegally. visa policy is an important lever at the disposal of the union and must be used to encourage third countries to cooperate on return.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, allow me a moment to say a few words on behalf of the committee on which i have worked, as my last speech to the libe committee in this parliament. we have done a lot in this parliament to help create a fair and supportive common european asylum system. we have done teamwork, smoothing out wherever possible our differences and trying to work on investing in our values. i will continue to do so, hoping for a just society, and i hope that the vote of the european people will enable me to continue along this path. we have a long way to go. after four years of intensive negotiations, we can now say with some pride that the european union has a common visa policy. and so i want to thank the committee i served on, the libe committee. a policy which is an integral part of the creation of an area without internal frontiers and which remains an essential instrument for facilitating travel, whether for economic or leisure reasons. a policy that creates growth and must be consistent with other union policies, such as those relating to external relations, trade, education, culture and tourism. we have managed to simplify procedures, contain costs and identify precisely which member state is competent to examine an application, particularly when the applicant intends to visit several member states. i would like to thank the commission for the work it has done in this area. we have provided for the possibility for applicants to submit application forms online and to be able to sign them electronically. and above all, we have safeguarded the right of appeal for applicants whose visas have been refused. four years of lengthy negotiations have enabled this reform to remain within a legal framework which guarantees full respect for fundamental rights.
member of the commission. – mr president, thank you for this very important debate. the new regulation will modernise the common visa policy so that security is preserved while legitimate travel is facilitated. it will ensure equal treatment for all visa applicants and promote travel to the european union for tourism and business purposes. in that way it will contribute to the european union’s economy and growth, people-to-people contacts and cultural exchanges. but beyond that, the new rules will enhance our ability to detect threats and will provide us with a stronger framework for cooperation with non-european union countries when it comes to the return and readmission of irregular immigrants. i strongly hope you will support the compromise reached on the new european union visa code in the vote. i can assure you that, from our side, the commission will play its role in the implementation of these new provisions.

the regulation we are supporting fills a serious gap by establishing for the first time in europe, after much resistance, after more than ten years of debate, common limits and standards on co2 emissions from heavy duty vehicles, which account for 6% of the total emissions in the union, and which are destined to increase. in addition to ambitious but achievable co2 reduction targets, we have introduced a road compliance test to obtain real driving emissions and fuel consumption data. these real data are often very far from those certified in the laboratory. this data is necessary to avoid other scandals like the diesel gate. these data may also be used by third parties for independent verification testing. the commission is also asked to provide a methodology for assessing the emissions of heavy-duty vehicles throughout their life cycle, from design to scrapping. the regulation also provides for a mechanism to incentivise the uptake of electric and low-emission trucks, with the aim of ensuring a mandatory minimum share of 2% of these vehicles for manufacturers from 2025. the commission will also assess the impact of the new rules on the market for electric vehicles and the impact of the new rules on the market for electric vehicles. finally, in the transition to decarbonisation of the transport sector, which is still 94% dependent on oil, the role of natural gas must be considered, but above all it is essential that the european commission establishes a fund for the retraining and support of workers in the sector, in order to make the transition socially and environmentally sustainable. this regulation is a further step in the process of moving europe towards a new model of development based on the alliance between industry and the environment.

member of the commission. – mr president, tonight’s debate on the investeu programme in the last plenary session is emblematic of the continued backing this house has given to the commission’s initiatives in support of investment throughout its mandate. on behalf of the commission, let me thank you for your support. the partial agreement you have reached with the council on investeu, in a record time, will allow for preparatory work to proceed quickly. this will ensure a smooth and timely implementation on day one of the next multiannual financial framework (mff), allowing for a seamless continuation of investment support. investeu will simplify our existing set of financial instruments and, under a single guarantee, rule book and brand, cater for sectors that are experiencing investment gaps and sub-optimal investments situations. digitisation, social housing, research, energy efficiency and urban transport are just some of the key areas that today don’t find adequate financing on the market. the investeu guarantee will unlock such financing and crowd-in private money for the public good. to deliver its objectives, the fund will be supported by investeu’s advisory hub that this house wants to strengthen. the commission welcomes this emphasis. the commission also highly values the fact that the co-legislators have upheld its proposal for an opening of access to the eu budgetary guarantee. while the european investment bank’s strategic role is now enshrined in the regulation and its expertise is better recognised, other actors such as international financial institutions like the ebrd or the council of europe bank, but also national promotional banks and institutions, will have the opportunity to become implementing partners. this will ensure we are using all available expertise in a complementary manner, improving their geographical outreach and taking into account local needs. the preparation of the investeu programme and its implementation will bring those actors together, require them to set up the system, but also give them the opportunity to take ownership and co-shape the union investment programme. this will result in a community of strong, long-term investors supporting the eu’s policy objectives. during the negotiations, the parliament has had a key role in maintaining the focus of this instrument on policy steer, in strengthening the accountability and transparency provisions, and in raising ambitions for the climate targets. the commission believes that all of these points improve investeu. let me conclude by expressing our appreciation for the tremendous effort of the rapporteurs, their shadows and all associated committees in reaching a position within a very ambitious timeline, with a view to enabling an agreement before the european elections. i would also like to take this opportunity to extend this appreciation to the romanian presidency for their dedication and effort.

the reporter. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is a real pleasure to present to this house the result of long and intensive work and negotiations, which have, however, produced positive results. i would like to thank my fellow rapporteur, josé manuel fernandes, all the shadow rapporteurs and all the colleagues who have helped to adopt this text, which continues a process which began five years ago. the financial crisis, the austerity policies had caused an unprecedented fall in public and private investment across the european union and one of our priorities was to revive it. more investment as a condition for growth and employment. thanks to a flexible interpretation of the stability pact and then to new initiatives such as the european fund for strategic investments, we have started a correction of the direction of economic policy, but new important investment gaps have opened up in the areas related to innovation, tangible, intangible and social infrastructure and climate change. these are the key challenges we intend to tackle with the investeu programme. in addition to further strengthening support for small and medium-sized enterprises, research, innovation and sustainable infrastructure, this programme will address the huge gap in social infrastructure, ensuring the real feasibility of projects in the fields of education, health and social housing. the agreement we reached with the council makes a number of improvements to the commission's text. first, we have established that the cost of the guarantee to the promoters of the investment will be exclusively linked to the characteristics and risk profile of the underlying transactions and that more favourable conditions can be applied to promote the construction of investment platforms, to encourage investment in areas where the investment gap is higher or to encourage intervention in those sectors where the need for investment is more pronounced. secondly, while recognising a special partnership, a central role for the european investment bank, we have emphasised the important role of national promotional banks in financing investment projects. national promotional banks will be able to have direct access to the european guarantee, which will allow greater flexibility and therefore greater possibilities for financing projects, with positive effects on the level of investment and the creation of new jobs. finally, we have established that member states will not only have the possibility of channelling part of their allocated resources under the cohesion policy funds into investeu in the national sector, but they will also be able to contribute additional resources which will, in principle, be considered as one-off contributions and therefore not calculated in the structural deficit account under the stability pact. the text we are voting on tomorrow is therefore a balanced text overall, including the important part which requires at least 55% of the investment under the sustainable infrastructure window which contributes to achieving the objectives of the paris climate and environment agreements. of course, a framework of certainty of resources is essential and so our commitment in the next legislature will be to negotiate a multiannual financial framework that is commensurate with this project, the ambitions of investeu but also the overall need for a strong european budget. we know that investeu will be an important, necessary but not sufficient part of what will be our political priority in the next legislature: implement an extraordinary investment programme to support the conversion, the ecological conversion of the economy, social sustainability, the revival of growth, innovation and employment.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the advent of new technologies is changing all the world's scenarios, including mobility. we must seize the challenge and the benefits if europe is to be a world leader in this field. the declarations and the fulfilments that have to be made each time a ship calls at a port are many and it is therefore necessary to streamline this formality and it is essential to introduce a single interface for those declarations. there is currently a complete lack of harmonisation between member states, which causes heavy administrative burdens for operators. this single interface will finally reduce these burdens, improving interoperability and interconnection between the different systems and encouraging maximum efficiency in the use of data. i would also like to take this opportunity to thank the commissioner and her staff for their excellent work, to thank my colleagues and, since we are the europe of the peoples, to also offer a greeting in slovenian, nasvidenje in hvala, and a greeting in friulian, which is also a greeting in friulian, my language, and thanks to dut con un mandi.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, shipping companies are currently subject to too many requirements and have to make different declarations each time a ship calls at a port. the main problem is the lack of harmonisation of reporting requirements across sectors and across countries, which unfortunately entails considerable additional costs for industry. the commission estimates that shipping personnel currently spend a total of some 4.6 million hours per year on reporting activities, which is too much. a single reporting interface for ships will significantly reduce these administrative burdens, further facilitating trade, digitalisation and modernising maritime mobility. this regulation creates the conditions for the application of the one-off principle so that ships can make one declaration in one port and reuse that information for subsequent calls in ports of the european union.
